rationale: PINS the haskell analyzer's FP-family surface against probe-verified tree-sitter-haskell shapes (2026-09-03): module header + export list, qualified imports (references edges), data/record/newtype constructors + record-field properties, deriving implements, superclass context extends, instance implements (incl. list-parametrized []), operator-definition symbols (a +.+ b / (<!>)), backtick calls, $-application calls, where-local resolution, record-CONSTRUCTION instantiates with the record-UPDATE negative, per-symbol complexity (case/conditional/guards), and evidence tiers (structural/import_based/usage_contextual). Negatives: relabel's record update emits NO instantiates; no fabricated calls to imported names (M.lookup emits the qualified call, nothing for Data.Text members). HSD12/14/16/18/19 wave (2026-09-03 re-review): standalone deriving (bare/qualified/parens class heads), qualified constructor application instantiates, pattern-position negatives (record-pattern head, case alternatives, pattern guard), tuple-head backtick definition (defined function, no self-call), constructor-pattern bind variables are NOT symbols. #872 ANALYZER HALF (added 2026-09-25, found by the hledger full-extent depth draw): the fixture always carried a TUPLE context class (`class (Show a, Eq a) => Mergeable2 a`) and pinned NOTHING about it, while the analyzer emitted ZERO extends for every list-context and every qualified superclass — so the two mutants minted to guard #872 (`haskell/drop-tuple-superclass`, `haskell/apply-head-as-argument`) both recorded `0 -> 0` in F4 while the lane read clean. Now pinned: BOTH members of a tuple, a QUALIFIED head taken VERBATIM (`Csv.ToNamedRecord`, the text the oracle derives), a tuple mixing bare and qualified members, and an APPLIED head resolved to its LEFT SPINE — `Eq (f a) => Applied f a` gives Applied -> Eq and never Applied -> f a, which is the class one of those mutants names and which did not exist in this fixture.

expectSymbols.name: UserId
expectSymbols.comment: dimension 8, SAME NAME at a second line. `instance Mergeable UserId` at 61 publishes a symbol named after its TARGET TYPE, so it collides by name with the `newtype UserId` at 29. It carries kind `instance`, NOT `class`: an instance is named after the type it instantiates, so containing it asserts this module DECLARES that type. Suppressed 176 such `contains` edges over the three corpora. The relationship that IS a fact about this module is `implements UserId -> Mergeable @61`.

M60-HK: a module import is an `imports` edge. It was published as `references` with evidenceClass=import_based, which made 2,119 of the lane's 2,126 `references` edges a mislabel — only 7 were genuine references.
M60-HK: a LATER import statement, so the relabel is not a first-import accident.

M60-HK: the export list is the module's API surface. The names were already collected into ctx.exports but never published as edges. `User(..)` normalises to the type it exports, not to a second name.
M60-HK: a value export, as distinct from the type export above.

M60-HK: `type Alias = Text` USES Text. `uses` and not `references`: this is a synonym composed from a type, not a body referring to a name. A type PARAMETER in the RHS would be a fabrication and is excluded.

M60-HK: `instance Mergeable UserId` overrides the class method. `overrides` was in the audited label set with ZERO rows on BOTH sides, so the audit compared nothing to nothing and read green — the exact failure the allowlist records for perl.

REVISED. `merge` is a member of the CLASS `Mergeable`, not of the type `UserId` that `instance Mergeable UserId` instantiates — ownership moved to the class. Containment is emitted only when the owner is DECLARED in this module, which keeps this true local case (both `class Mergeable` and the instance are here) while dropping the far more common foreign-class body, e.g. `instance Applicative Reference` no longer claims this module declares `Applicative` or `pure`. The `implements UserId -> Mergeable @61` edge is what records that this module instantiates UserId.

dimension 8, REVISED. This group was pinned at 2 because the file has two same-named children of Data.User: the `newtype UserId` at 29 and the `instance Mergeable UserId` at 61. The instance now carries kind `instance` and no longer emits `contains`, because an instance is named after the type it INSTANTIATES — containing it asserted this module DECLARES `UserId`. Only the newtype is declared here, so the count is 1. The instance is still covered, as a symbol (`kind: instance` at 61) and by `implements UserId -> Mergeable @61`. The multi-site group remains pinned, so `haskell/edge-line-per-set` still cannot collapse it unnoticed.

M60-HK: the export list INTERLEAVES Haddock comments with exports. Iterating every named child published them as exported names — 39 edges whose target was a `--` comment. A comment is not a name and no consumer can resolve it. The target is spelled exactly as the corpus defect produced it (`exports Hasql.Decoders -> "-- * Result"`) so the matching mutant is CAUGHT rather than surviving on a near-miss string.
